tasks.short: Plan and lay out a repair from drawings and manuals.

steps.what: Read the repair fault on the maintenance work order
Retrieve drawings, blueprints and schematic diagrams for the asset
Draft a checklist from the maintenance manual section

loop.purpose: Draft a short checklist from the named maintenance manual section.
loop.input: The fault line and the text of the named manual section.
loop.output: A checklist draft of steps and warnings.
loop.check: The worker checks that each drafted line restates a sentence in that manual section, and rejects a line that adds a step or a warning the section does not state.
loop.stop: No manual section is linked to the asset, or the worker rejects the draft.
loop.why_not_simpler: The manual is free text and the pages differ by asset, so a fixed form cannot pick the lines.

steps.what: Walk the plant and lay out the repair against the drawings
Choose the repair sequence the site layout showed

tasks.design: The repair work order in the {OTHER} maintenance system carries the asset id, the fault and, when known, the manual section. The current drawings open from {DOCS} for that asset, and a bounded reading of the manual section drafts a checklist the worker checks against the manual sentences. The worker still walks the plant and marks the repair layout; the draft is not the layout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings sat in cabinets or in unsorted files, and a checklist still had to be copied by hand from a manual the worker had to find.
tasks.enabler_now: A work order can hold an asset id, and a reading of free-text manual pages can draft a checklist a person reviews against those pages.
tasks.still_hard: The plant often differs from the drawing, and only the person on site can see that.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a pipe, a wall or a machine does not match the drawing, and choosing a sequence that is safe to start.

ambition.what: Which drawing revision matches the asset, before the walk, including plants whose folder sits in another building.

tasks.altitude: The worker still walks the plant and marks the layout. The morning starts with the current drawing and a checklist draft open, and the right to reject both stays with the worker.

reach.learn: Which drawing revision the layout used, and which manual lines the worker rejected.

evidence.claim: A procedure generator can draft a checklist from a maintenance procedure, and a person reviews it before release.
Comparing a drawing to the installed pipes, machines and structure is a site visit. A drafted checklist does not see the plant. Model knowledge.
Work orders that store time stamps or location can observe technicians, and Dutch works-council consent is required first.
Annex III covers a system that allocates crew work by behaviour or traits, or that monitors performance. Drafting a checklist from a manual is outside that case.

assumptions: The planner's work order already holds asset id, fault text, and a manual section id when one exists. If the section id is missing, the worker picks the manual by hand and the draft step stops.
Drawings in the document store are filed by asset id and revision. A paper-only drawing stays a cabinet fetch, and that time stays in the retrieval step.
The checklist draft is not the layout. The worker confirms each line against the manual sentences, not against an identifier match alone.
This design adds no location trail and no score of the worker. Isolation permits and parts spend are a different task.
Test the maintenance system's own link to the document store before any custom integration.
unknowns: What share of assets has a current drawing filed by asset id.
Whether the works council has already consented to time stamps on maintenance work orders.
research_questions: How often the installed plant differs from the latest drawing on file.
Which manual sections are free text rather than a fixed checklist.

already_counted.description: Check the opened fault and asset line before fetching drawings.
Check the retrieved drawing is the revision fitted on the asset.
Check each checklist line against the manual sentences and reject added steps.

incremental.description: Relink a manual section when the asset document is replaced, and clear rejected checklist drafts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A month where half the assets still have only a paper drawing in a cabinet, so retrieval barely shrinks, and the checklist draft is rejected whenever the manual section is old. The walk and the sequence choice stay as they are.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train maintenance personnel or manage subcontractors on the job.

steps.what: Read which maintenance personnel are on shift
Decide which personnel or subcontractors to train or manage
Train personnel or manage subcontractors beside the job
Write who was trained and which procedure was practised

tasks.design: The day's jobs and the people on shift are read from the {OTHER} maintenance work orders. The worker still decides whom to train or direct, and still does that beside the job. Afterward a line in {DOCS} stores the person, the procedure and the date, with no score and no location.
tasks.previous_blocker: The only record of who was shown a job was memory or a signed paper in the workshop.
tasks.enabler_now: A short form on the work order can store person, procedure and date after the training. The training itself is unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: People learn by doing the job next to someone, and a form does not show whether they can do it.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a person or a subcontractor has understood the job in front of them.
tasks.altitude: The worker still trains and directs people on the job. Nothing about who may direct a subcontractor changes. A one-line register is written after the training.

reach.learn: Which procedure was practised on site and who was directed.

evidence.claim: Training a person or directing a subcontractor on the job is in-person work. A register can store the person, the procedure and the date, and it does not show whether they can do the job. Model knowledge.
Allocating crew work by behaviour or traits, or monitoring performance, is the Annex III case. Choosing who to train stays a person's decision.
A work order that stores time stamps or location can observe technicians, and Dutch works-council consent is required first.

assumptions: The shift list holds name and role only. The training line stores person, procedure name and date. It does not store a score, a location or a start and stop time.
Extra spend, a new subcontract or a variation is a purchasing task, not this one. Directing a subcontractor already on site is an internal direction.
Who is trained is chosen by the worker. No rule and no model assigns people by past speed or by ratings.
Upkeep of the form is the small allowance below. There is no separate admin baseline.
unknowns: Whether subcontractors are allowed to be named in the internal training register.
Whether a procedure list already exists for this site or must be typed as free text.
research_questions: How often a new subcontractor arrives without having seen the site procedure.
Whether supervisors already keep a paper training signature that this line would replace.

already_counted.description: Read the opened shift list and match it to today's jobs.
Check the training line names the person and the procedure just practised.

incremental.description: Correct a training line when the procedure name was wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of new subcontractors, where the briefing stays fully in person, and the register is still a paper line when the workshop device is not at the job.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The maintenance worker still walks the plant, marks the layout, and trains people beside the job. Opening the current drawing and writing a training line take less of the morning. No new right to assign work by a score, and no new right to change a drawing.
reach: Maintenance planner: which drawing revision the layout used, and which manual lines were rejected.
First-line supervisor: which procedure was practised and who was directed on site.
skills_to_grow: Match a drawing revision to the plant in front of them
Reject a checklist line the manual does not state
Write a training line without scoring the person
role.ambitious_version: The current drawing and a checklist draft open with the job, and the worker rewrites them only when the plant disagrees. Training stays beside the job, with one line recorded after.
